# Motivation: functional data in large epidemiological studies



## National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)

![](figs/nhanes.png)

::: {.notes}
Large, nationally representative survey of over 15,000 ppts every two years
2011-2014: collected high freq accel data from 7 days, in addition to health, nutrition, etc.
:::

::: {.notes}

We're statisticians - we want to quantify this difference - we need to fit a model! 

::: 


## Function on scalar regression (FoSR)

<div style="font-size: 115%;">


Model: $$\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{PA}_i(s)] = \beta_0(s) + \beta_1(s)\mathbb{I}\{\mathrm{sex}_i=\mathrm{female}\} + \sum_{k=2}^{7}\beta_k(s)\mathbb{I}\{\mathrm{agecat}_i=k\} $$ 

$i$: participant; 

$s \in \{1, \dots, 1440\}$: each minute of the day


</div>

::: {.notes}
Outcome: steps profile over the course of the day (function) 

Predictors: age, sex (scalars)

Interpretation
  $\beta_0(s)$: expected steps for reference sex category and reference age category
   Can be interpreted at specific points of the day (e.g., how many more steps do males take at 12pm, holding age constant

:::

## FoSR: model fitting 

::: {.incremental}

<div style="font-size: 150%;">
+ Fast univariate inference (FUI) [@Cui2021]

+ Fit separate (univariate) GLM at each point $s$, smooth the resulting point estimates 

+ Bootstrap subjects to get confidence bands 

</div>

:::

::: {.notes}

Could also fit with penalized splines

:::

# Gap: no method to adjust for survey design

## NHANES is not a random sample! 

![](figs/nhanes_sample.gif)

Individuals sampled in geographic clusters, minority groups oversampled 

Are estimates from FoSR valid for population-level inference? 

**No** method exists for function on scalar regression under complex surveys

<div style=" position: absolute; bottom: -1em; left: 10em; font-size: 0.6em; color: #777; "> [NHANES Sample Design Tutorial](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/tutorials/sampledesign.aspx) </div>

# What if we combine some existing methods? 

## Survey function on scalar regression 

<div style="font-size: 135%;">


::: {.incremental}



+ Standard regression: methods and software to take into accounts weights and correlation between clusters ($\texttt{svyglm}$, $\texttt{svycoxph}$) [@surveys] for estimation and inference


+ FUI is built on separate GLMS

+ **Idea**: incorporate survey weights into the GLMs (estimation) and use survey-aware replication/bootstrap methods for inference 

:::

</div>

# Implementation

## Fit survey-weighted GLM at each point along the functional domain 




## What about inference? 

<div style="font-size: 135%;">

::: {.incremental}

+ Can't use the standard errors from weighted GLMs because: 
  + Correlation between strata/clusters
  + Correlation across the functional domain 

::: 

</div>

## Inference: survey-aware replication methods 

Use balanced repeated replication (BRR) [@BRR] to obtain $B$ sets of survey weights, fit model on each set

```{r brr vis}
#| cache: true 

sample_structure = tibble(
  sample_type = rep(c("Full Sample", "Replicate 1", "Replicate 2", "Replicate 3", "Replicate 4", "Replicate B"), each = 4),
  stratum = rep(1:4, 6),
  unit1 = rep(TRUE, 24),
  unit2 = rep(TRUE, 24)) |> 
  mutate(
    unit1 = case_when(
      sample_type == "Replicate 1" ~ FALSE,
      sample_type == "Replicate 2" ~ stratum %in% c(2, 4),
      sample_type == "Replicate 3" ~ stratum %in% c(3, 4),
      sample_type == "Replicate 4" ~ stratum %in% c(2, 3),
      sample_type == "Full Sample" ~ TRUE,
      sample_type == "Replicate B" ~ TRUE
    ),
    unit2 = case_when(
      sample_type == "Replicate 1" ~ TRUE,
      sample_type == "Replicate 2" ~ stratum %in% c(1, 3),
      sample_type == "Replicate 3" ~ stratum %in% c(1, 2),
      sample_type == "Replicate 4" ~ stratum %in% c(1, 4),
      sample_type == "Full Sample" ~ TRUE,
      sample_type == "Replicate B" ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("unit"), names_to = "unit", values_to = "included")

ggplot(sample_structure %>% filter(included), 
       aes(x = unit, y = factor(stratum), fill = unit)) +
  geom_tile(color = "#f6f5f3", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~sample_type, ncol = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("unit1" = "#65CCFFFF", "unit2" = "#FFCC65FF"),
                    labels = c("Unit 1", "Unit 2")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("1", "2")) +
  labs(title = "Balanced Repeated Replication Schematic",
       y = "Stratum", x = "Cluster", fill = "Cluster") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

```

## Inference: survey-aware replication methods 

Use pointwise variance to get pointwise confidence intervals

```{r ci vis}
#| cache: true 


male_vec = unname(male_vec)
fit = gam(male_vec ~ s(seq_along(male_vec), bs = "tp", k = 20), method = "GCV.Cp")

male_smooth = fitted(fit)

male_smooth |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  mutate(s = row_number(),
         var = var_smooth,
         lower = value - 1.96 * sqrt(var_smooth),
         upper = value + 1.96 * sqrt(var_smooth)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = s, y = value, color = var)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, x = s), alpha = .5) +
  geom_point(size = .3, alpha = .5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1440, 240),
                     labels = c("00:00", "04:00", "08:00", "12:00", "16:00", "20:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Difference in MIMS: Males minus Females",
       title = "Estimated coefficient and pointwise 95% confidence intervals") +
  scale_color_paletteer_c("ggthemes::Red-Gold", name = "Pointwise Variance") +
  theme(legend.position = c(.75, .75)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, 1.1)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "slategrey")

  
```

## Joint inference 

<div style="font-size: 135%;">

::: {.incremental}

+ We are doing 1440 correlated tests for significance
+ How can we adjust our CIs to take into account correlation $and$ multiplicity? 

::: 

</div>

## Joint inference 

Bonferroni: $\alpha = 0.05 / 1440 = 3.47\cdot10^{-5}; z_{1-\alpha/2}=3.98$


```{r bonferroni}
#| cache: true 
q = qnorm(1-3.472222e-05)
# bonferroni correction 
male_smooth |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  mutate(s = row_number(),
         var = var_smooth,
         lower = value - 1.96 * sqrt(var_smooth),
         lower2 = value - q * sqrt(var_smooth),
         upper = value + 1.96 * sqrt(var_smooth),
         upper2 = value + q * sqrt(var_smooth)) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = s, ymin = lower2, ymax = upper2, fill = "Bonferroni adjusted"), color = NA) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = s, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = "Pointwise"), color = NA) +
  geom_smooth(data = mdf, inherit.aes = FALSE, aes(x = s, y = value),
              method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "tp", k = 21), se = FALSE, 
              color = "black") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1440, 240),
                     labels = c("00:00", "04:00", "08:00", "12:00", "16:00", "20:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Difference in MIMS: Males minus Females",
       title = "Estimated coefficient and 95% confidence intervals") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "#0072B2FF"), name = "") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "slategrey") +
  theme(legend.position = c(.75, .75)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, 1.1))

```

## Joint inference 


<div style="font-size: 135%;">


Bonferroni is conservative: we know that points close on the functional domain are correlated 

</div> 

## Joint inference: CMA 

**Key insight:** $\hat{\mathbf{f}} = \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ is multivariate normal 

$$\hat{\mathbf{f}} \approx N(\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{\hat{V}}_f)$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{V}}_f = \mathbf{X}\hat{\mathbf{V}}_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \mathbf{X}^t$





## Joint inference: CMA 

**Key insight:** $\hat{\mathbf{f}} = \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ is multivariate normal 

$$\hat{\mathbf{f}} \approx N(\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{\hat{V}}_f)$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{V}}_f = \mathbf{X}\hat{\mathbf{V}}_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \mathbf{X}^t$


**Standardize:** 

$$\frac{(\hat{\mathbf{f}} - \mathbf{f})}{\mathbf{D}_f} \approx N(\mathbf{0}_n, \mathbf{C}_f)$$

where $\mathbf{D}_f = \sqrt{\text{diag}(\hat{\mathbf{V}_f)}}$ and $\mathbf{C}_f$ is the correlation matrix





## Joint inference: CMA 

**Key insight:** $\hat{\mathbf{f}} = \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ is multivariate normal 

$$\hat{\mathbf{f}} \approx N(\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{\hat{V}}_f)$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{V}}_f = \mathbf{X}\hat{\mathbf{V}}_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \mathbf{X}^t$


**Standardize:** 

$$\frac{(\hat{\mathbf{f}} - \mathbf{f})}{\mathbf{D}_f} \approx N(\mathbf{0}_n, \mathbf{C}_f)$$

where $\mathbf{D}_f = \sqrt{\text{diag}(\hat{\mathbf{V}_f)}}$ and $\mathbf{C}_f$ is the correlation matrix


**CMA:** Find $q(\mathbf{C}_f, 1-\alpha)$ such that

$$P\{-q(C_f, 1-\alpha) \times e \leq X \leq q(C_f, 1-\alpha) \times e\} = 1-\alpha$$

where $X \sim N(\mathbf{0}_n, \mathbf{C}_f)$


## Joint inference: CMA 

Bonferroni critical value = $3.98$; CMA critical value = $3.03$


```{r cma}
#| cache: true 
qn = model$cis$qn[2]
# bonferroni correction 
male_smooth |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  mutate(s = row_number(),
         var = var_smooth,
         lower = value - 1.96 * sqrt(var_smooth),
         lower3 = value - qn * sqrt(var_smooth),
         upper3 = value + qn * sqrt(var_smooth),
         lower2 = value - q * sqrt(var_smooth),
         upper = value + 1.96 * sqrt(var_smooth),
         upper2 = value + q * sqrt(var_smooth)) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = s, ymin = lower2, ymax = upper2, fill = "Bonferroni adusted"), color = NA) + geom_ribbon(aes(x = s, ymin = lower3, ymax = upper3, fill = "Correlation and multiplicity adjusted (CMA)"), color = NA) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = s, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = "Pointwise"), color = NA) +
  geom_smooth(data = mdf, inherit.aes = FALSE, aes(x = s, y = value),
              method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "tp", k = 21), se = FALSE, 
              color = "black") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1440, 240),
                     labels = c("00:00", "04:00", "08:00", "12:00", "16:00", "20:00", "24:00")) +
  labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Difference in MIMS: Males minus Females",
       title = "Estimated coefficient and 95% confidence intervals") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "#56B4E9FF", "#0072B2FF"), name = "") +
  theme(legend.position = c(.75, .85)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, 1.1)) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "slategrey") 


```

# Easy enough to implement -- but how do we know if it works? 

## Simulation goal

::: {.incremental}

+ Generate a superpopulation of individuals who belong to a stratum and cluster 
+ Each individual has functional outcome and covariate
+ [Optionally] create correlation in functional outcomes within strata and clusters
+ [Optionally] create heterogeneity in covariate effects by strata/cluster
+ Sample from the superpopulation in each iteration of the simulation
  + [Optionally] allow for informative sampling: probability of being included in sample related to functional outcome 

:::

## Data generating


```{r}
#| cache: true
btrue_df %>% 
  mutate(name = factor(name, 
                       levels = c("(Intercept)", "X"),  # adjust to your actual levels
                       labels = c("beta[0](s)", "beta[1](s)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = s, y = beta, color = name)) + 
  facet_grid(.~name, labeller = label_parsed) + 
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + 
  labs(x = "Functional domain", 
       y = "Value", 
       color = "", 
       title = "Global intercept and slope functions") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text = element_text(family = "sans")  # Use default font for Greek
  ) +
  scale_color_paletteer_d("ggthemes::colorblind", direction = -1)

```

## Data generating: add stratum-specific covariate effects 

$\beta_{1(h)}(s) = \gamma_h\cdot\beta_1(s)$

Where $\gamma_h \sim N(1, 0.125^2)$

```{r strata specific slopes}
#| cache: true 

b1_strat_df |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(strata, scale),
               names_to = "l", 
               names_transform = ~as.integer(sub(".*V", "", .x))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = l, y = value, color = scale, group = strata)) + 
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_paletteer_c("ggthemes::Red-Gold") +
  labs(x = "Functional Domain", y = "Value", title = expression(beta[1(h)](s))) +
  geom_line(data = btrue_df |> filter(name == "X") |> mutate(strata = 1), 
            aes(x = s, y = beta, linetype = "Global Slope"), 
            color = "#2B5C8A", linewidth = 1.1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    name = "", 
    values = "dashed",
    labels = expression("Global slope " * beta[1](s))
  ) +
  labs(x = "Functional Domain", y = "Value", title = expression(beta[1(h)](s))) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.2, 0.7),
        title = element_text(family = "sans"),
        legend.text = element_text(family = "sans", size = 14)) +
  guides(color = "none")
```


## Data generating: induce strata and cluster-level correlation with functional random effects

Generate strata-level ($b_{h(i)}(s)$) and cluster-level ($b_{c(h, i)}(s)$) random effects using B-spline basis 

Individual-level linear predictor: 
$\eta_i(s) = \beta_0(s) + X_i\beta_{1(h)}(s) + b_{h(i)}(s) + b_{c(h, i)}(s)$

```{r re plot}
#| cache: true
re_df |>
  filter(strata %in% c(1:10),
         psu %in% psu_df$x) %>%
  group_by(strata, psu) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("V"),
               names_to = "ind",
               names_transform = ~as.integer(sub(".*V", "", .x))) %>%
  mutate(strata = paste0("Stratum ", strata),
         strata = factor(strata, levels = paste0("Stratum ", seq(1:10)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ind, y = value, color = factor(psu))) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, linewidth = .7) +
  facet_wrap(~strata, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Functional Domain", y = "Value", title = "Random effects by stratum and cluster") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "A")
```

## Survey sampling: sample individuals from superpopulation 
1. Sample 2 clusters from each stratum
2. Sample individuals from each cluster 
3. Informative sampling: allow selection probability to depend on functional outcome: $\pi_i \propto \frac{1}{L}\sum_{s=1}^LY_i(s)$

```{r plot surv wts}
#| cache: true
mean_df %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_spaghetti(aes(y = Y_mean_strat, color = quant), linewidth = 2, alpha = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Selection probability tertile",
                     values = c("#FF2B00FF", "#FF9933FF", "#002BFFFF"),
                     labels = c("Highest third", "Middle third", "Lowest third")) +
  labs(x = "Functional domain", y = "Smoothed functional outcome", title = "Selection probability and functional outcomes under informative sampling") 
```

```{r compare}
#| cache: true 
plt_ov = 
  plt_df |> 
  mutate(model = "BRR") |> 
  bind_rows(plt_df_unwtd |>  mutate(model = "Unweighted")) |> 
  mutate(var_name = if_else(grepl("Male", var_name), "Male", "Intercept"))

disagree_df =
  plt_ov %>%
  select(lower_joint, upper_joint, var_name, model, l) %>%
  mutate(sig = case_when(
    lower_joint > 0 & upper_joint > 0 ~ 1,
    upper_joint < 0 & lower_joint < 0 ~ 1,
    .default = 0
  )) %>%
  select(var_name, model, l, sig) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = sig) %>%
  mutate(brr_sig = BRR == 1 & Unweighted == 0,
         disagree = BRR != Unweighted) %>%
  filter(disagree) 

annotation_data = tibble(
  var_name = "Male",
  x_label = c(3 * 60, 21 * 60),  # Left and right sides
  y_label = c(-1.5, -1.7),
  x_arrow_start = c(3 * 60, 18 * 60),
  x_arrow_end = c(1.5 * 60, 16.2 * 60),
  y_arrow_end = c(-1.8, -2),
  label = c("Only unweighted\njointly significant",
          "Only survey-aware\njointly significant"),
  color = c("#CC79A7FF", "#009E73FF"),
  hjust = c(0, 1)  # Left-align first, right-align second
)

ggplot(plt_ov, aes(x = l, y = beta_hat, group = model)) +
    facet_wrap(. ~ var_name, scales = "free_y") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(x = l, ymin = lower_pw, ymax = upper_pw, fill = model), alpha = .5) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(x = l, ymin = lower_joint, ymax = upper_joint, fill = model), alpha = .3) +
    geom_line(aes(color = model), linewidth = 1.1)  +

    labs(x = "Time of Day", y = "Coefficient Estimate", fill = "Model Type", color = "Model Type") +
```

## Computation 

<div style="font-size: 115%;">

::: {.incremental}

+ NHANES model ($B = 500$, $n = 1200$, $L = 1440$) takes under 4 minutes to run on standard computer 
+ Speedups:
  + If predictors $X$ are same across functional domain, instead of fitting a separate model at each time point, we can create $n\times L$ matrix $Y$ by stacking our outcomes and fit $B = (X'WX)^{-1}X'WY$
  + Use QR decomposition instead of calculating $(X'WX)^{-1}$ directly
  + For GLMs, apply above at each step of IRLS or Newton-Raphson 
  + Parallelize bootstrapping 

::: 

</div>

# References
